title: Focus-wheel interface authoring through Wright
summary: Normal Wright workspace and actual isolated engineering run. No mocked routes or physical action.

manualSteps.label: Open workspace
manualSteps.instruction: Open the isolated Repeated focus-wheel preparation proof workspace.

manualSteps.label: Open workflows
manualSteps.instruction: Click Workflows in the workspace activity bar.

manualSteps.label: Choose process
manualSteps.instruction: Click Workflow files, then Open workflow. Select the saved focus-wheel workflow.

manualSteps.label: Use process
manualSteps.instruction: Click Use saved process. Reopen the recorded run from its workspace link.

manualSteps.label: Create an interface
manualSteps.instruction: Click Create or choose interface. Enter Focus-wheel configured preparation as the Interface title and request a reusable comparison with shared inputs, results, findings and review controls. Click Update selected interface.

manualSteps.label: Preview
manualSteps.instruction: Wait for Preview ready, then click Open preview and inspect the read-only interface.

manualSteps.label: Save
manualSteps.instruction: Return to the common working tab and click Save interface.

manualSteps.label: Open saved interface
manualSteps.instruction: Click Open saved interface. Confirm it opens in a Wright workspace tab on the existing run.

steps.label: Workspace offers Workflows
steps.purpose: Verify the normal workspace route with real API owners.
steps.action: Open Repeated focus-wheel preparation proof workspace.
steps.expected: The workspace loads and offers Workflows.
steps.actual: Normal workspace and Workflows control visible.

steps.label: Workflows opens the editor
steps.summary: The established workflow editor is available inside the workspace.
steps.purpose: Verify actual workspace entry without mocking.

steps.label: Workflow file controls
steps.summary: The workspace offers named saved workflows.
steps.purpose: Use the existing saved file chooser.

steps.label: Choose the focus-wheel workflow
steps.summary: The exact accepted focus-wheel workflow appears in the saved files.
steps.purpose: Choose the engineering process by its saved file.
steps.expected: The accepted focus-wheel workflow is listed.

steps.label: Focus-wheel workflow diagram
steps.summary: The original focus-wheel assignment opens with its connected review, geometry and slicing stages.
steps.purpose: Keep authoring and working views on the accepted source.
steps.action: Choose the accepted focus-wheel workflow file.
steps.expected: Accepted focus-wheel diagram and working view action available.
steps.actual: Exact saved focus-wheel source is open.

steps.label: Shared working view
steps.summary: The process working interface opens in another Wright workspace tab.
steps.purpose: Verify shared inputs and readiness without creating another executor.
steps.expected: Common working view in a workspace tab.

steps.label: Attach the actual focus-wheel run
steps.summary: The working view reads the same isolated backend run.
steps.purpose: Use actual process state for interface composition.
steps.action: Reopen the recorded focus-wheel run link.
steps.expected: The common working view attaches without starting another run.

steps.label: Wright interface authoring
steps.summary: The process exposes Wright�s shared interface creation controls.
steps.purpose: Author the tailored experience through Wright, within the workspace.
controls: How should this interface help the user?
steps.expected: Native authoring controls tied to this exact process.

steps.label: Visible interface creation
steps.summary: Wright is creating the tailored interface using its actual configured default model.
steps.action: Enter Interface title: Focus-wheel configured preparation. Request: Make a focused update to the supplied previous source. Retain the heading and responsive evidence grid; add this exact concise limitation beside results: Digital geometry and slice evidence do not establish fit, strength or physical print acceptance. Preserve all shared inputs/readiness, progress, pending interactions, diagnostics, assessment and result/evidence/producing-block navigation callbacks and ResultRepresentation viewers. Use only the backend interaction contract for the engineering-review hold; do not invent retry actions, accepted verdicts, measurements, an executor or protocols. Keep new manifest identities and parent revision; bind across runs without fixed paths or run IDs. Return only required source/manifest JSON.. Click Update selected interface.
controls: How should this interface help the user?
steps.expected: Accepted job and visible generation progress.
steps.actual: Actual focused update accepted; creation progress visible.

steps.label: Built comparison ready
steps.summary: The actual generated interface has passed Wright�s fixed local build.
steps.purpose: Inspect the built preview before saving.
steps.expected: Successful built revision ready for preview.

steps.label: Managed focus-wheel preparation preview
steps.summary: The actual generated comparison renders in a Wright tab with read-only preview controls.
steps.purpose: Inspect the generated UI and its actual backend evidence.
steps.expected: Isolated managed preview renders and reads the process contract.

steps.label: Reusable focus-wheel interface saved
steps.summary: The previewed interface is retained as a versioned process asset.
steps.purpose: Save the exact checked source, bindings and build.
steps.action: Return to the common tab and click Save interface.
steps.expected: The exact previewed revision is saved.
steps.actual: Interface saved with its built revision.

steps.label: Saved focus-wheel preparation opens
steps.summary: The saved working interface opens within Wright and reads the existing run.
steps.purpose: Open saved built assets without UI regeneration.
steps.expected: Saved working interface connected to the same process/run.
steps.actual: Saved comparison is connected in a workspace tab.
